summary: Describes an RTP payload format for Enhanced AC-3 audio, a high-quality multichannel format that extends AC-3 and is used in broadcast and disc systems. It is a standards-track document.

eli5.summary: This explains how to cut a high-quality surround sound stream into small pieces that can be sent over the internet in real time.

questions: what is e-ac-3 rtp payload format
how are e-ac-3 frames fragmented in rtp
subtitle: How to chop Dolby's multichannel E-AC-3 audio into RTP packets for streaming over IP networks.

tldr.problem: Enhanced AC-3 (E-AC-3) is a multichannel audio format used in television and disc systems, and there was a need to stream it over IP networks, including frames too big for one packet.
tldr.mechanism: Each RTP payload starts with a two-byte header, then carries whole E-AC-3 frames or one fragment of a frame. A media type, audio/eac3, and an optional bitStreamConfig parameter describe the programs and substreams for SDP.
tldr.outcome: E-AC-3 audio can be sent with RTP's timing and synchronization, for uses such as IPTV and video on demand. Confidentiality and authentication are left to external mechanisms such as SRTP.

today: RFC 4598 is a Proposed Standard from July 2006. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why Stream E-AC-3
sections.content:
Enhanced AC-3 (E-AC-3) is an extension of the AC-3 audio coding standard, which is commonly used for DVD, broadcast, cable and satellite television. It is designed to work at both higher and lower data rates than AC-3 and to support more channels. Dolby Digital Plus is a branded version of it.

E-AC-3 is mostly used for audio that goes with video, so RTP, with its mechanism for synchronizing streams, is a good fit. The RFC lists IPTV, video on demand, interactive features of next generation DVD formats and moving movies across a home network as target uses.
sections.eli5: Movies have rich surround sound. This document explains how to send that sound over the internet so it stays lined up with the picture.

sections.title: What E-AC-3 Looks Like
sections.content:
E-AC-3 is a frequency-domain perceptual coder: it removes audio information that people are unlikely to hear. It runs at data rates from 32 kbps to 6.144 Mbps and at sampling rates of 32 kHz, 44.1 kHz and 48 kHz. E-AC-3 content is not directly compatible with AC-3 decoders, but it can be converted to AC-3.

The basic building block is the sync frame. A frame holds Sync Information, Bit Stream Information, an Audio Frame field, up to six audio blocks, and an optional auxiliary field and a CRC. Each audio block represents 256 PCM samples per channel, and a frame carries one, two, three or six blocks.

A bit stream holds up to eight programs. Each program has one independent substream, carrying up to 5.1 channels that can be decoded alone, and up to eight dependent substreams that add channels. A decoder must be able to decode at least the first independent substream of the first program and ignore the rest.
sections.eli5: Think of a song split into short slices. Each slice is a frame. A basic slice plays fine alone, and extra slices can add more speakers for people with fancier setups.

sections.title: RTP Header and Payload Header
sections.content:
The RTP payload type is not set by this document; it comes from the RTP profile or is signaled out-of-band, for example with SDP. The marker (M) bit is set to one when the packet holds at least one complete frame or the final fragment of a frame. The timestamp corresponds to the sampling instant of the first frame in the packet. Packets with fragments of the same frame MUST have the same timestamp. The first timestamp SHOULD be random and then grows by the number of samples per frame, with 256 samples per block.

Every payload MUST begin with a two-byte payload header: a MBZ field that is set to zero and ignored by receivers, a one-bit F field, and an eight-bit NF field. If F is 0, the payload holds one or more complete frames and NF is the number of frames. If F is 1, the payload holds a fragment and NF is the number of fragments that make up the frame. NF MUST be identical for all fragments of a frame.

When a packet holds several frames, the receiver uses the frmsiz field in each frame's header to find where the next one starts, because frame length can vary.
sections.eli5: Each packet starts with a tiny note saying either how many whole slices are inside, or that this is one piece of a slice that was cut up and how many pieces there are.

sections.title: Fragmenting and Packing Frames
sections.content:
An E-AC-3 frame counts as one application data unit, and a payload carries a whole number of complete frames or a single fragment. If a frame is bigger than the network MTU, it SHOULD be fragmented at the RTP level. The split MAY be made at any byte boundary, and the packets with fragments of one frame SHALL be sent in consecutive order, first to last.

When frames are small, several can share a packet. To limit the damage from a lost packet, frames from more than one program set SHOULD NOT share a packet unless all program sets in it are complete, and the same holds for frame sets. A frame set is the group of frames covering six consecutive audio blocks, which lines E-AC-3 up with AC-3 framing.

AC-3 frames can also appear inside an E-AC-3 stream, but only in the independent substream of the first program. A receiver of this format MUST also be able to receive the AC-3 payload format of RFC 4184.
sections.eli5: Big slices are cut into pieces that are sent in order. Small slices can ride together in one packet, but it is best if a packet holds complete groups, so losing one packet does not ruin its neighbors.

sections.title: Media Type and SDP Usage
sections.content:
The RFC registers the media type audio/eac3. The required parameter rate is the RTP clock rate and equals the sampling rate: 32000, 44100 or 48000. The optional parameter bitStreamConfig describes the bit stream as one letter per substream (i for independent, d for dependent) followed by the number of channels that result when it is decoded. An LFE channel counts as one, so 5.1 is written as 6. For example, i6d8d14i6d8 describes two programs.

In SDP, the subtype goes in a=rtpmap, the rate is the clock rate, and bitStreamConfig goes in a=fmtp. In an offer/answer exchange, an answerer can put 0 for any substream it does not want to receive. To stay interoperable, an E-AC-3 end-point SHOULD also declare itself AC-3 capable, and a sender of AC-3 in the E-AC-3 format SHOULD also offer the AC-3 payload format.
sections.eli5: Before the show starts, the two sides trade a short code listing which sound tracks they will send or want. A side can say no thanks to the extra ones by writing 0.

sections.title: Security and Congestion
sections.content:
The format inherits the security considerations of RTP (RFC 3550) and any RTP profile. Confidentiality, integrity protection and authentication have to come from a mechanism outside the payload format, for example SRTP. The E-AC-3 format lets decoders check the validity of frames, and the required response to a malformed frame is to discard it and conceal the error until a valid frame is decoded.

The usual congestion control considerations for RTP apply. Because E-AC-3 is a variable bit rate coding system, a variety of techniques can be used to adapt to network bandwidth. IANA registered the new media subtype.
sections.eli5: Locking the audio so nobody can listen in or tamper with it is a separate job done by other tools. The decoder simply skips broken pieces.

fields.name: MBZ
fields.desc: Must be zero; ignored by receivers; reserved for future extensions.

fields.name: F
fields.desc: 0 for one or more complete frames, 1 for a fragment of a frame.

fields.name: NF
fields.desc: Number of frames, or number of fragments that make up the frame.
